POSITIONS.md:57
- P-59 **Walk chooses a coercion by the run-time value until it runs the checker, after the switch-over.** Walk has no static types. So where a coercion is needed, walk chooses it by the value's run-time type. The specification and the compiled path choose it by the static type. The curator accepts this as the interpreter's limit, and walk is not changed for it before the switch-over. A callout in the coercion chapter (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex`) states the limit. Two expected-failure tests record it: `XXXCoercionStaticRungC`, the chapter's own printed example, and `XXXCoercionStaticNarrowRungC`. After the switch-over, once walk runs the checker on its programs (P-12 orders the two steps), it uses the static coercions that the checker inserts.

== explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md, ## The goal

POSITIONS.md:12
- P-12 **After the switch-over, walk runs the compiled type checker on its programs, and then uses the static coercions that the checker inserts.** The curator wants the checker usable on the programs that walk runs. Today `fortress typecheck` checks a program only against the compiler's prelude, so it is no check of walk's programs (F-9 holds this fact). Walk is not changed for this before the switch-over. After it, walk runs the checker on its programs and so gains their static types; F-9 and F-290 say what walk and the library lack for that step. Walk then uses the static coercions that the checker inserts, in place of its choice on the run-time value (P-59, walk's choice of coercions until the switch-over).

== explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md, ## Decisions on record, ### The one library and the compiled checker

POSITIONS.md:62
- P-148 **The checker's speed comes right after its correctness in priority: a rung that changes the compiled checker also makes the change fast.** The rung times the checker before and after its change. It first makes the change correct. Then, in the same rung, it makes the new code fast, without changing which programs the checker accepts or refuses. So no optimization is left to be done by hand after the landing. Why: the checker must stay usable as it grows. Some slowdown is fine, but new checks have made it orders of magnitude slower, so that the checker ran past the time limit of the batch gate's count stage, and rungs could not land. The timing is a smoke test: one run of each tree, to catch a slowdown of several times; a small difference is noise. The `fortress-repo` skill (`compiler.md`, "The checker's time") gives the steps, their commands and what the rung reports.

POSITIONS.md:35
- P-37 **One library, the interpreter's, is the library that the compiler checks.** The interpreter's prelude, `FortressLibrary` and `FortressBuiltin`, becomes the compiled path's prelude in place of the compiler's own, and the compiled path reads the interpreter's library with it. Why: the switch-over spares porting the interpreter's library into the compiler's; the revival develops the checker until it accepts that fuller library. The curator sees the compiler's prelude, its own library files `CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerBuiltin` and `CompilerAlgebra`, as a bootstrap to remove. == Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:500-705

\section{Coercion Resolution}
\seclabel{resolving-coercion}
For a given functional call, we first determine whether there exists a
declaration that is applicable without coercion.  If so, the most
specific declaration is selected; if not, then coercions are
explicitly added to the functional call.  If more than one coercion is
possible then the coercion that yields the most specific type is
chosen.  \secref{restrictions-coercion} and
\chapref{overloaded-declarations} describe overloading rules for the
declarations of coercions and overloaded functionals that guarantee
there exists always a most specific coercion when two or more are possible.
A declaration with static parameters is applicable, without or with coercion,
when some instance of it whose static arguments satisfy their bounds is, and
declarations are compared on the parameter types they declare
(\secref{functional-applicability}, \secref{resolving-overloading}); the
declaration selected is then instantiated as \secref{static-arg-inference}
describes, with the rule for a numeral whose conversions tie
(\secref{numeral-default}).
\revision{revival-overloading}{The Working Draft of February 2011 did not say
here when a declaration with static parameters is applicable.
The revival decided on 28~September 2026 that a coercion makes a call possible
and never changes which declaration runs when one is applicable without it:
declarations are chosen in the order this section gives, on the parameter types
they declare, and the declaration chosen is then instantiated.}

We first define a notion of more specific types in the presence of coercion.
Recall from \secref{type-relations} that Fortress defines an
\emph{exclusion} relation between types which is denoted by $\excludes$.

For types $T$ and $U$, we say that $T$ \emph{rejects} $U$,
and write $T \rejects U$, if for all coercions to $T$, the type coerced
from excludes $U$:
\[
T \rejects U \iff \forall A: A \coercedefto T \implies A \excludes U.
\]
Note that $T \rejects U$ implies $U \not\coercesto T$.

We say that $T$ is \emph{no less specific} than $U$, and write $T
\morespecificeq U$, if $T$ is a subtype of $U$ or $T$ excludes, can be
coerced to, and rejects $U$:
\[
T \morespecificeq U \iff
T \Ovrsubtype U \logicor
(T \excludes U \logicand T \coercesto U \logicand T \rejects U).
\]

The $\morespecificeq$ relation is reflexive and antisymmetric but not
necessarily transitive.  It is possible, for example, for
three types, $T$, $U$ and $V$, each excluding the other two,
to have coercions from $T$ to $U$ and from $U$ to $V$.  In
this case, $T \morespecificeq U$ and $U \morespecificeq V$ but
$T \not\morespecificeq V$.

Notice that if two tuple types have a bijective correspondence
between their element types then the $\morespecificeq$ relationship between
the tuple types is equivalent to applying the $\morespecificeq$
relation elementwise.

We say that $T$ is \emph{more specific} than $U$, and write $T
\morespecific U$, if $T \morespecificeq U \logicand T \neq U$.

We extend the definitions of no less specific and more specific to
declarations.  We say that a declaration $\f(\Ps)$ is \emph{no less
specific} than a declaration $\f(\Qs)$ if $\Ps \morespecificeq \Qs$.
Similarly, we say that a declaration $\Ps_0.\f(\Ps)$ is \emph{no less
specific} than a declaration $\Qs_0.\f(\Qs)$ if $(\Ps_0, \Ps)
\morespecificeq (\Qs_0, \Qs)$.  A declaration $\f(\Ps)$ is \emph{more
specific} than a declaration $\f(\Qs)$ if $\Ps \morespecific \Qs$.
Similarly, a declaration $\Ps_0.\f(\Ps)$ is \emph{more specific} than
a declaration $\Qs_0.\f(\Qs)$ if $(\Ps_0, \Ps) \morespecific (\Qs_0,
\Qs)$.

Now we describe how to determine which coercion is applied to a given
call in terms of rewriting functional calls.  The rewriting is
for pedagogical purposes; implementation techniques may vary.

Consider a static call $\f(\As)$ or $\As_0.\f(\As)$.  Let $\Sigma$ be
the set of parameter types of functional declarations of $\f$ that are
applicable to the call.
Let $\Sigma'$ be the set of parameter types of
functional declarations of $\f$ that are
applicable with coercion to the call.
If $\Sigma$ is not empty then we use the overloading resolution
described in \secref{resolving-overloading} to determine which
element of $\Sigma$ is called.
The parameter type of a declaration with static parameters is in $\Sigma$, or
in $\Sigma'$, when some instance of the declaration whose static arguments
satisfy their bounds is applicable to the call, without or with coercion; the
static arguments of the declaration selected are inferred afterwards
(\secref{static-arg-inference}).
\revision{revival-overloading}{The Working Draft of February 2011 did not say
when the parameter type of a declaration with static parameters is in these
sets.}
If $\Sigma$ is empty but $\Sigma'$ is not, then we rewrite the call as
follows.  Define: \[\mathpzc{C} = \{T \in \Sigma' \mid S \coercedefto T
\logicand \As \Ovrsubtype S\}.\] Let $T \in \mathpzc{C}$ be the most
specific element of $\mathpzc{C}$.  In other words, there does not exist
$T' \in \mathpzc{C}$ such that $T' \morespecific T$.  The restrictions
given in \secref{restrictions-coercion} and
\chapref{overloaded-declarations} guarantee that such a $T$
exists and that it is unique.  The call $\f(\As)$ or $\As_0.\f(\As)$ is
rewritten to \EXP{f(\mathrm{coercion}\llbracket{T}\rrbracket(\TYP{A}))} or
\EXP{A_{0}.f(\mathrm{coerce}\llbracket{T}\rrbracket(A))}
and the declaration with parameter
type $T$ is applied to the call.

As an example, consider the following definitions:
%trait ZZ32 excludes { ZZ64, ZZ128 } end
%trait ZZ64 excludes { ZZ128 }
%  coerce(z:ZZ32) = ...
%end
%trait ZZ128
%  coerce(z:ZZ32) = ...
%  coerce(z:ZZ64) = ...
%end
%
%f(z:ZZ64) = 1
%f(z:ZZ128) = 2
\begin{Fortress}
\(\KWD{trait} \mathbb{Z}32 \KWD{excludes} \{\,\mathbb{Z}64, \mathbb{Z}128\,\} \KWD{end}\)\\
\(\KWD{trait} \mathbb{Z}64 \KWD{excludes} \{\,\mathbb{Z}128\,\}\)\\
{\tt~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(  \KWD{coerce}(z\COLONOP\mathbb{Z}32) = \ldots\)\-\\\poptabs
\(\KWD{end}\)\\
\(\KWD{trait} \mathbb{Z}128\)\\
{\tt~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(  \KWD{coerce}(z\COLONOP\mathbb{Z}32) = \ldots\)\\
\(  \KWD{coerce}(z\COLONOP\mathbb{Z}64) = \ldots\)\-\\\poptabs
\(\KWD{end}\)\\[4pt]
\(f(z\COLONOP\mathbb{Z}64) = 1\)\\
\(f(z\COLONOP\mathbb{Z}128) = 2\)
\end{Fortress}

declaration \EXP{f(\mathbb{Z}64)} because $\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}
\morespecific \EXP{\mathbb{Z}128}$, which follows from the facts that
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} excludes \EXP{\mathbb{Z}128}, coerces to it, and rejects it:
the one type that coerces to \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, excludes
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}128}.
The same facts make the two declarations of \VAR{f} a valid overloading, and the
exclusion of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} by \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} does the same for the two
coercions to \EXP{\mathbb{Z}128} (\secref{more-specific-rule}).
\revision{revival-coercion-example}{The Working Draft of February 2011 declared the
three traits with no \KWD{excludes} clause and said that the resolution follows
from the fact that \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} coerces to \EXP{\mathbb{Z}128}.
By the definition above, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} is then not more specific than
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}128}, and neither the two declarations of \VAR{f} nor the two
coercions to \EXP{\mathbb{Z}128} are a valid overloading; both implementations
of the revival refuse the example as the Working Draft wrote it.
The clauses added are spelled as \library\ spell those of their integer types,
each trait excluding the wider ones.}

Notice that coercion is resolved statically.  Once a coercion is
statically chosen for a call, this coercion is conceptually inserted
into the call.
This means that the statically chosen coercion is applied at run time.
The coercions that the instance of a declaration with static parameters needs
are chosen and inserted into the call in the same way
(\secref{static-arg-inference}).
\revision{revival-overloading}{The Working Draft of February 2011 did not say
how the coercions of an instance of a declaration with static parameters are
chosen.}

%end

\(f(a\COLONOP{}A) = 3\)\\
\(f(b\COLONOP{}B) = 4\)\\[4pt]
\(c \mathrel{\mathtt{:}} C = D\)\\
\(f(c)\)
\end{Fortress}

\EXP{f(A)} despite the fact that the declaration

\EXP{f(B)} is
%dynamically directly

120	  /**
121	   * Given an arrow type, an expected type context, and a list of partitioned args (where Left is
122	   * checked and Right is an unchecked arg (usually an anonymous function)), determine if the arrow is applicable to these args.
123	   * This method will infer static arguments on the arrow and parameter types on any FnExpr args.
124	   * The result is an AppCandidate, which contains the inferred arrow type, the list of static
125	   * args that were inferred, and the checked arguments.
126	   */
127	  def checkApplicable(preCandidate: PreAppCandidate,
128	                      context: Option[Type],
129	                      args: List[Either[Expr, FnExpr]],
130	                      mOpName: Option[Op],
131	                      coerce: Boolean = false,
132	                      promote: Option[List[StaticArg]] = None)
133	                     (implicit errorFactory: ApplicationErrorFactory)
134	                      : Either[AppCandidate, OverloadingError] = {
135	    val arrow = preCandidate.arrow
136	
137	    // Make sure all uncheckable args correspond to arrow type params.
138	    zipWithDomain(args, arrow.getDomain).foreach {
139	      case (Right(_), pt) if !possiblyArrows(pt, getStaticParams(arrow)) =>
140	        return Right(errorFactory.makeNotApplicableError(arrow, args))
141	      case _ =>
142	    }
143	
144	    // Infer lifted static params.
145	    val argType = getArgType(args)
146	    /* If we are checking an operator we need to get the name of the overloading in order
147	     * to check if it is a parametric operator
148	     */
149	    val mOpNames = mOpName match {
150	      case Some(opName) => 
151	        // If we are checking an operator the overloading in preCandidate should be some
152	        val PreAppCandidate(_, Some(ovName), _) = preCandidate // DRC breakpoint
153	        Some((opName, ovName.getOriginalName.asInstanceOf[Op]))
154	      case None => None
155	    }
156	    // The op parameter corresponding to a parametric operator must be lifted
157	    val (liftedArrow, liftedSargs) =
158	      inferLiftedStaticParams(arrow, argType, mOpNames).getOrElse{
159	        return Right(errorFactory.makeNotApplicableError(arrow, args))
160	      }
161	
162	    // Are there static params? i.e., do we need more inference?
163	    val candidateOrError =
164	      if (hasStaticParams(liftedArrow))
165	        if (coerce || promote.isDefined)
166	          checkApplicableWithCoercion(liftedArrow, preCandidate, context, args, promote)
167	        else checkApplicableWithInference(liftedArrow, preCandidate, context, args) match {
168	          // A static argument that a numeral fixes at the numeral's own type is
169	          // left to the attempt with coercion, which reads the numeral by its
170	          // default, where that attempt can check the call: where no argument
171	          // is a function expression still unchecked.
172	          case Left(c) if args.forall(_.isLeft) && numeralFixesOwnType(c, args) =>

175	        }

179	    // If applicable, then inject the lifted static args into the result.

185	  /**
186	   * Check that the arrow type is applicable to these args with static argument
187	   * inference and no coercion.
188	   */
189	  def checkApplicableWithInference(
190	          arrow: ArrowType,
191	          preCandidate: PreAppCandidate,
192	          context: Option[Type],
193	          args0: List[Either[Expr, FnExpr]])
194	          (implicit errorFactory: ApplicationErrorFactory)
195	           : Either[AppCandidate, OverloadingError] = {
196	
197	    val originalArrow = preCandidate.arrow
198	    val args = preDefault(arrow, context, args0)
199	
200	    // Try to check the unchecked args, constructing a new list of
201	    // (checked, unchecked) arg pairs.
202	    def updateArgs(argsAndParam: (Either[Expr, FnExpr], Type))
203	                     : (Either[Expr, FnExpr], Option[BodyError]) = argsAndParam match {
204	
205	      // This arg is checkable if there are no more inference vars
206	      // in the param type (which must be an arrow).
207	      case (Right(unchecked), paramType:ArrowType) =>
208	        if (hasInferenceVars(paramType.getDomain))
209	          (Right(unchecked), None)
210	        else {
211	
212	          // Try to check the arg given this new expected type.
213	          inferFnExprParams(unchecked, paramType, false) match {
214	            // Move this arg out of unchecked and into checked.
215	            case Left(checked) => (Left(checked), None)
216	            // This arg might be checkable later, so keep going.
217	            case Right(bodyError) => (Right(unchecked), Some(bodyError))
218	          }
219	
220	        }
221	
222	      // If the parameter type is not an arrow, skip it.
223	      case (Right(unchecked), _) => (Right(unchecked), None)
224	
225	      // Skip args that are already checked.
226	      case (Left(checked), _) => (Left(checked), None)
227	    }
228	
229	    // Update all args until we have checked as much as possible.
230	    def recurOnArgs(args: List[Either[Expr, FnExpr]])
231	                    : Either[AppCandidate, OverloadingError] = {
232	
233	      // Build the single type for all the args, inserting the least arrow
234	      // type for any that aren't checkable.
235	      val argType = getArgType(args)
236	
237	      // Do type inference to get the inferred static args.
238	      val (resultArrow, sargs) =
239	        inferStaticParams(arrow, argType, context).getOrElse {
240	          return Right(errorFactory.makeNotApplicableError(originalArrow, args))
241	        }
242	
243	      // Match up checked/unchecked args and param types and try to check the unchecked args,
244	      // constructing a new list of (checked, unchecked) arg pairs.
245	      val newArgsAndErrors = zipWithDomain(args, resultArrow.getDomain).
246	                               map(updateArgs)
247	      val (newArgs, maybeErrors) = (newArgsAndErrors).unzip
248	
249	      // If progress was made, keep going. Otherwise return.
250	      if (newArgs.count(_.isRight) < args.count(_.isRight))
251	        recurOnArgs(newArgs)
252	      else {
253	
254	        // If not all args were checked, gather the errors.
255	        if (newArgs.count(_.isRight) != 0) {
256	          return Right(makeOverloadingError(originalArrow,
257	                                            resultArrow.getDomain,
258	                                            newArgsAndErrors))
259	        }
260	
261	        // If there are inference variables left, inform the user that there
262	        // wasn't enough context.  A size left unknown is an error only where it
263	        // reaches a type or a static argument of this call.
264	        if (hasInferenceVars(resultArrow) || hasSizeInferenceVars(sargs)) {
265	          val unfixedSize =
266	            if (hasSizeInferenceVars(sargs) && !hasInferenceVars(resultArrow.getDomain))
267	              Some(AppCandidate(resultArrow,
268	                                sargs,
269	                                newArgs.map(_.left.get),
270	                                preCandidate.overloading,
271	                                preCandidate.fnl))
272	            else None
273	          return Right(errorFactory.makeNoContextError(originalArrow, sargs, unfixedSize))
274	        }
275	
276	        // We've reached a fixed point and all args are checked!
277	        Left(AppCandidate(resultArrow,
278	                          sargs,
279	                          defaultAtUnfixedEach(newArgs.map(_.left.get), resultArrow.getDomain),
280	                          preCandidate.overloading,
281	                          preCandidate.fnl))
282	      }
283	    }
284	
285	    // Do the recursion to check the args. A declaration that only a numeral's
286	    // default at a parameter of its default type made applicable, and whose
287	    // size the call then leaves unknown, is checked as the numeral is.
288	    recurOnArgs(args) match {
289	      case Right(NoContextError(_, _, Some(_))) if !(args eq args0) => recurOnArgs(args0)
290	      case r => r
291	    }
292	  }

294	  /**
295	   * Check that the arrow type is applicable to these args with static argument
296	   * inference and coercion. The static args are inferred from the args whose
297	   * parameter types mention a static parameter other than as the whole type,
298	   * and from the context. A type parameter that is the whole type of a
299	   * parameter and appears in no other parameter type takes the narrowest type,
300	   * under the coercion chapter's no-less-specific relation, among its args'
301	   * types, the types they coerce to, its declared bound and the intersection
302	   * of its upper bounds (its declared bound, Any if none, and what the context
303	   * requires), that each of its args is substitutable for; where numerals
304	   * alone fix it and no one type is narrowest, the numerals are read as ZZ32
305	   * (ZZ64 or ZZ by magnitude). Every

307	   * or by a coercion. With `promote`, the static args inference by subtyping
308	   * found: only a type parameter they bind to a union is chosen again.
309	   */
310	  def checkApplicableWithCoercion(
311	          arrow: ArrowType,
312	          preCandidate: PreAppCandidate,
313	          context: Option[Type],
314	          args: List[Either[Expr, FnExpr]],
315	          promote: Option[List[StaticArg]])
316	          (implicit errorFactory: ApplicationErrorFactory)
317	           : Either[AppCandidate, OverloadingError] = {
318	    def notApplicable = Right(errorFactory.makeNotApplicableError(preCandidate.arrow, args))
319	    if (args.exists(_.isRight)) return notApplicable
320	    val checked = args.map(_.left.get)
321	    val params = getStaticParams(arrow).filter(!_.isLifted)
322	    // The order in which inferStaticParams returns the static args.
323	    val order = params.filter(_.getDominatesClause.isEmpty) ++ params.filterNot(_.getDominatesClause.isEmpty)
324	    val names: Set[IdOrOp] = params.map(_.getName).toSet
325	    val typeNames: Set[IdOrOp] = params.filter(_.getKind.isInstanceOf[KindType]).map(_.getName).toSet
326	    def mentioned(t: Type): Set[IdOrOp] = {
327	      var found = Set[IdOrOp]()
328	      object finder extends Walker {
329	        override def walk(node: Any): Any = node match {
330	          case n: VarType if names(n.getName) => found += n.getName; node
331	          case n: IntRef if names(n.getName) => found += n.getName; node
332	          case _ => super.walk(node)
333	        }
334	      }
335	      finder(t); found
336	    }
337	    def bare(d: Type): Option[IdOrOp] = d match {
338	      case v: VarType if typeNames(v.getName) => Some(v.getName)
339	      case _ => None
340	    }
341	    // An argument whose trait's comprises clause lists one type at where-clause
342	    // sizes (TypeAnalyzer.opensSizes) is opened once for the call, so that its
343	    // admission below meets the size its inference bound; a subtype check would
344	    // open it afresh.
345	    def opened(t: Type): Type = t match {
346	      case tt: TraitType if analyzer.opensSizes(tt) => analyzer.comprisedTypes(tt) match {
347	        case Some(cs) if cs.size == 1 => cs.head
348	        case _ => t
349	      }
350	      case _ => t
351	    }
352	    val argTypes = checked.map(e => opened(normalize(getType(e).get)))
353	    val positions = zipWithDomain(argTypes, arrow.getDomain)
354	    val numerals = zipWithDomain(checked, arrow.getDomain).map(p => isNumeral(p._1))
355	    val fixedElsewhere = positions.filter(p => bare(p._2).isEmpty).flatMap(p => mentioned(p._2)).toSet
356	    val chosen = positions.flatMap(p => bare(p._2)).distinct.filterNot(fixedElsewhere)
357	    def valueOf(sargs: List[StaticArg], n: IdOrOp): Option[Type] =
358	      order.zip(sargs).collectFirst { case (sp, STypeArg(_, _, t)) if sp.getName == n => t }
359	    def own(n: IdOrOp): List[(Type, Expr)] =
360	      positions.zip(checked).collect { case ((t, d), e) if bare(d) == Some(n) &&
361	        !t.isInstanceOf[BottomType] && !hasInferenceVars(t) => (t, e) }
362	    // The types a chosen parameter may take: its args' types, the types they
363	    // coerce to, and its declared bound. None leaves it to its upper bounds.
364	    def named(n: IdOrOp): List[Type] = {
365	      val ts = own(n).map(_._1)
366	      val bound = params.find(_.getName == n).toList.
367	                    flatMap(sp => toListFromImmutable(sp.getExtendsClause)).

369	                                !Set("Object", "Any")(b.asInstanceOf[TraitType].getName.getText))
370	      val all = (ts ++ ts.flatMap(coercions.getCoercionTargetsFrom(_)) ++ bound).distinct
371	      // A numeral's own type is no static argument that the numeral fixes.
372	      if (own(n).exists(p => NumeralConversion.isNumeral(p._2))) all.filterNot(isNumeralType) else all
373	    }
374	    // A parameter that numerals alone fix, with no expected type, takes the
375	    // narrowest default that holds them all; where no candidate is found so,
376	    // it is chosen as any other parameter.
377	    def numeralsAlone(n: IdOrOp) = own(n).nonEmpty && own(n).forall(p => NumeralConversion.isNumeral(p._2))

379	    def choicesOf(useDefault: Boolean): List[List[Option[Type]]] = chosen.map { n =>
380	      promote match {
381	        case Some(sargs) => valueOf(sargs, n) match {
382	          case Some(_: UnionType) => None :: named(n).map(Some(_))
383	          case v => List(v)
384	        }

388	    }

392	      choices.foldRight(List(List[Option[Type]]())) { (cs, acc) => for (c <- cs; m <- acc) yield c :: m }

411	        else numeralJoinInto(e, p).orElse(coercions.buildCoercion(e, p)).orElse(defaultFits(e, p)).getOrElse(return None)
412	      }
413	      val newArgTypes = newArgs.zip(checked.zip(argTypes)).map { case (n, (e, a)) => if (n eq e) a else getType(n).get }
414	      if (!isSubtype(NF.makeMaybeTupleType(NF.typeSpan, toJavaList(newArgTypes)), resultArrow.getDomain)) return None
415	      Some(AppCandidate(resultArrow, sargs, newArgs, preCandidate.overloading, preCandidate.fnl))
416	    }
417	    val found = combos.flatMap(attempt(_)) match {
418	      case Nil if byDefault =>
419	        val plain = combosOf(choicesOf(false))
420	        if (plain.size > 64) return notApplicable
421	        plain.flatMap(attempt(_))
422	      case f => f
423	    }
424	    def noWider(a: AppCandidate, b: AppCandidate) = chosen.forall { n =>
425	      (valueOf(a.sargs, n), valueOf(b.sargs, n)) match {
426	        case (Some(s), Some(t)) => coercions.noLessSpecific(s, t)
427	        case _ => false
428	      }
429	    }
430	    def narrowest(cs: List[AppCandidate]) = cs.find(a => cs.forall(noWider(a, _)))
431	    narrowest(found).orElse {
432	      // A parameter that numerals alone fix, with no one type narrowest: the
433	      // numerals are read as ZZ32, or as ZZ64 or ZZ by magnitude.
434	      val byNumerals = chosen.filter(n => own(n).nonEmpty && own(n).forall(p => isNumeral(p._2)))
435	      if (byNumerals.isEmpty) None
436	      else {
437	        val readings = byNumerals.map(n => numeralReading(own(n).map(_._2)))
438	        if (readings.exists(_.isEmpty)) None
439	        else narrowest(found.filter(c => byNumerals.zip(readings.map(_.get)).forall { case (n, r) =>
440	                 valueOf(c.sargs, n).exists(coercions.substitutableFor(r, _)) }))
441	      }
442	    } match {
443	      case Some(c) => Left(c)
444	      case None => notApplicable
445	    }
446	  }

448	  /**
449	   * Whether the expression is a numeral, with or without a radix point, or a
450	   * size used as a value, which the checker types as one.
451	   */
452	  def isNumeral(e: Expr): Boolean = getType(e) match {
453	    case Some(t) => Types.isNumeralType(t)
454	    case None => false
455	  }

457	  /**
458	   * The type numerals are read as when nothing narrower fixes them: ZZ32, or
459	   * ZZ64 or ZZ when a numeral's value does not fit, and RR64 when one has a
460	   * radix point; the supertype or coercion target of the numeral type with
461	   * that name.
462	   */
463	  def numeralReading(es: List[Expr]): Option[Type] = {
464	    val big = es.collect { case l: IntLiteralExpr => l.getIntVal }
465	    val point = es.exists(e => getType(e).exists(Types.isRadixPointNumeralType))
466	    val name =
467	      if (point) "RR64"
468	      else if (big.forall(v => v.bitLength < 32)) "ZZ32"
469	      else if (big.forall(v => v.bitLength < 64)) "ZZ64"
470	      else "ZZ"
471	    // The numeral types now carry each numeral's four numbers, so the targets
472	    // are found from one numeral's own type.
473	    val from = es.flatMap(e => getType(e).filter(Types.isNumeralType)).collect { case t: TraitType => t }.headOption.getOrElse(return None)
474	    (analyzer.ancestors(from).toList.collect { case t: TraitType => t } ++
475	     coercions.getCoercionTargetsFrom(from)).find(_.getName.getText == name)
476	  }

478	  /**
479	   * Check that the arrow type is applicable to these args without any static
480	   * argument inference. The resulting args may have coercions.
481	   */
482	  def checkApplicableWithoutInference(
483	          arrow: ArrowType,
484	          preCandidate: PreAppCandidate,
485	          args: List[Either[Expr, FnExpr]])
486	          (implicit errorFactory: ApplicationErrorFactory)
487	           : Either[AppCandidate, OverloadingError] = {
488	    
489	    val originalArrow = preCandidate.arrow
490	
491	    // Gather up either-args and option-errors.
492	    val newArgsAndErrors = zipWithDomain(args, arrow.getDomain).map {
493	
494	      // If `checked` is a subtype of the param type, use it. Otherwise, try to
495	      // build a coercion to the param type and use that. If it does not coerce
496	      // to the param type, this is a NotApplicableError.
497	      case (Left(checked), paramType) =>
498	        if (isSubtype(getType(checked).get, paramType))
499	          (Left(defaultAtUnfixed(checked, paramType)), None)
500	        else numeralJoinInto(checked, paramType).orElse(
501	             coercions.buildCoercion(checked, paramType)).orElse(defaultFits(checked, paramType)) match {
502	          case Some(coercion) => (Left(coercion), None)
503	          case None =>
504	            return Right(errorFactory.makeNotApplicableError(originalArrow, args))
505	        }
506	
507	      // For each unchecked FnExpr arg, try to infer its parameter type and
508	      // check it. We don't need to add coercions because arrow types don't have them.
509	      case (Right(unchecked), paramType:ArrowType) =>
510	        inferFnExprParams(unchecked, paramType, true).
511	          fold(checked => (Left(checked), None),
512	               err => (Right(unchecked), Some(err)))
513	
514	      // Unchecked FnExpr arg with a non-arrow parameter type -- error.
515	      case (Right(unchecked), _) =>
516	        return Right(errorFactory.makeNotApplicableError(originalArrow, args))
517	    }
518	
519	    // Make sure that all the args were checked. If any remain unchecked, gather
520	    // up all the inference errors into an overloading error.
521	    val (newArgs, maybeErrors) = arrow.getDomain match {
522	          case d:AnyType => (args.map {
523	                               case Left(e) => Left(defaultAtUnfixed(e, d))
524	                               case a => a
525	                             }, None)
526	          case _ => (newArgsAndErrors).unzip
527	        }
528	    if (newArgs.count(_.isRight) != 0) {
529	      Right(makeOverloadingError(originalArrow,
530	                                 arrow.getDomain,
531	                                 newArgsAndErrors))
532	    } else {
533	
534	      // We need to make sure there are the right number of args for the domain.
535	      // Now that coercions are in place, we can simply check if the new arg
536	      // type is a subtype of the domain type.
537	      val argType = getArgType(newArgs)
538	      if (isSubtype(argType,arrow.getDomain) && (newArgs.size == args.size))
539	        Left(AppCandidate(arrow,
540	                          Nil,
541	                          newArgs.map(_.left.get),
542	                          preCandidate.overloading,
543	                          preCandidate.fnl))
544	      else
545	        Right(errorFactory.makeNotApplicableError(originalArrow, args))
546	    }
547	  }

650	  /**
651	   * Type check the application of the given arrow candidates to the given args.
652	   * This returns the statically applicable candidates (with their corresponding
653	   * inferred static args and updated arguments) with the most specific one at
654	   * the head.
655	   *
656	   * The candidates are tried by subtyping without the context; failing that,
657	   * by subtyping with the context; failing that, with coercion and the
658	   * context; failing that, with coercion without it. So a candidate that fits
659	   * the call as it is is not passed over for one reached by coercion whose
660	   * result fits the context. An attempt by
661	   * subtyping counts only the candidates that fit without a coercion the call
662	   * needs, so that when none does, the attempt with coercion ranks every
663	   * candidate applicable with coercion, generic or not, a generic one on its
664	   * declared domain. An attempt is kept when the most specific candidate's
665	   * result converts to the context, so that a coercion of the result still
666	   * applies. A call no attempt accepts takes the first attempt with the
667	   * context that holds a candidate, and with `fallBackWithoutContext` the first
668	   * without it, so that the refusal is reported where and as it is without it. A
669	   * candidate inferred by subtyping whose static args bind a type parameter to
670	   * a union is instantiated by the promotion instead, and is ranked on its
671	   * declared domain with the promotion's coercions uncounted. A call with no
672	   * most specific candidate is an error when coercions are in the tie, unless
673	   * the tie is a numeral's, which the numeral read as ZZ32 settles.
674	   */
675	  def checkApplication(preCandidates: List[PreAppCandidate],
676	                       iargs: List[Expr],
677	                       context: Option[Type],
678	                       mOpName: Option[Op] = None,
679	                       fallBackWithoutContext: Boolean = false)
680	                      (implicit errorFactory: ApplicationErrorFactory)
681	                       : Option[List[AppCandidate]] =
682	    typedApplication(preCandidates, iargs, context, mOpName, fallBackWithoutContext).map(_._1)
683	
684	  /**
685	   * checkApplication with the call's type beside the candidates: the most
686	   * specific candidate's return type, or, for a tie among declarations without
687	   * static parameters that fit the call without coercion, in a family with no
688	   * declaration with static parameters, the intersection of the tied
689	   * candidates' return types. Such a tie arises where the argument's static
690	   * type sits between closed traits whose overlap other declarations cover;
691	   * the declaration that runs is below every tied one, and its return type
692	   * below each of theirs by the Return Type Rule.
693	   */
694	  def typedApplication(preCandidates: List[PreAppCandidate],
695	                       iargs: List[Expr],
696	                       context: Option[Type],
697	                       mOpName: Option[Op],
698	                       fallBackWithoutContext: Boolean)
699	                      (implicit errorFactory: ApplicationErrorFactory)
700	                       : Option[(List[AppCandidate], Type)] = {
701	
702	    // Check all the checkable args and make sure they all have types.
703	    val args = partitionArgs(iargs).getOrElse(return None)
704	    typedApplicationOfChecked(preCandidates, iargs, args, context, mOpName, fallBackWithoutContext, true)

707	  /**
708	   * typedApplication over its args checked without an expected type. With
709	   * `retry`, a call that no attempt keeps is tried by the argument retry
710	   * before the attempts' fallback.
711	   */
712	  def typedApplicationOfChecked(preCandidates: List[PreAppCandidate],
713	                                iargs: List[Expr],
714	                                args: List[Either[Expr, FnExpr]],
715	                                context: Option[Type],
716	                                mOpName: Option[Op],
717	                                fallBackWithoutContext: Boolean,
718	                                retry: Boolean)
719	                               (implicit errorFactory: ApplicationErrorFactory)
720	                                : Option[(List[AppCandidate], Type)] = {
721	
722	    // A candidate, with its declaration's arrow when it is compared on its
723	    // declared domain, and whether the promotion instantiated it.
724	    type Ranked = (AppCandidate, Option[ArrowType], Boolean)
725	    type Attempt = List[(Either[AppCandidate, OverloadingError], Option[ArrowType], Boolean)]
726	    def moreSpecific(a: Ranked, b: Ranked) = moreSpecificCandidate(a._1, b._1, a._2, b._2, a._3, b._3)
727	    def isUnion(sarg: StaticArg) = sarg match {
728	      case STypeArg(_, false, _: UnionType) => true
729	      case _ => false
730	    }
731	    def generic(pc: PreAppCandidate) = getStaticParams(pc.arrow).exists(!_.isLifted)
732	
733	    // Filter the overloadings that are applicable, by subtyping or with
734	    // coercion. A candidate without static parameters is checked alike in
735	    // every attempt, so it is checked once.
736	    val plain = scala.collection.mutable.Map[Int, (Either[AppCandidate, OverloadingError], Option[ArrowType], Boolean)]()
737	    def applicable(ctx: Option[Type], coerce: Boolean): Attempt = preCandidates.zipWithIndex.map { case (pc, i) =>
738	      if (getStaticParams(pc.arrow).isEmpty)
739	        plain.getOrElseUpdate(i, (checkApplicable(pc, ctx, args, mOpName, coerce), None, false))
740	      else checkApplicable(pc, ctx, args, mOpName, coerce) match {
741	        case Left(c) if !coerce && c.sargs.exists(isUnion) =>
742	          checkApplicable(pc, ctx, args, mOpName, false, Some(c.sargs.filter(!_.isLifted))) match {
743	            case Left(promoted) => (Left(promoted), Some(pc.arrow), true)
744	            case _ => (Left(c), None, false)
745	          }
746	        case Left(c) if coerce && generic(pc) => (Left(c), Some(pc.arrow), false)
747	        case e => (e, None, false)
748	      }
749	    }
750	    def candidatesOf(es: Attempt): List[Ranked] = es.collect { case (Left(c), d, p) => (c, d, p) }
751	    // A coercion the call needs, not one the promotion introduced.
752	    def counted(c: Ranked) = !c._3 && c._1.args.exists(NumeralConversion.counts)
753	    // An attempt by subtyping holds the candidates that fit the call without a
754	    // coercion it needs; an attempt with coercion holds all it finds.
755	    def holds(es: Attempt, coerce: Boolean) =
756	      if (coerce) candidatesOf(es).nonEmpty else candidatesOf(es).exists(!counted(_))
757	    def paramTypes(c: Ranked) = zipWithDomain(c._1.args, c._1.arrow.getDomain).map(_._2)
758	    def sameTypes(a: List[Type], b: List[Type]) =
759	      a.size == b.size && a.zip(b).forall(p => Formula.isTrue(analyzer.equivalent(p._1, p._2)))
760	    // The candidates no other candidate is more specific than.
761	    def minimal(cs: List[Ranked]) = new PartialOrder[Ranked](cs, moreSpecific).minimal
762	    val groundFamily = preCandidates.forall(pc => getStaticParams(pc.arrow).isEmpty)
763	    // The type of a tie among declarations without static parameters that fit
764	    // the call as it is, in a family without static parameters.
765	    def tieType(top: List[Ranked]): Option[Type] =
766	      if (groundFamily && top.size > 1 && !top.exists(counted) &&
767	          top.forall(c => c._2.isEmpty && !c._3 && c._1.sargs.isEmpty) &&
768	          !top.forall(c => sameTypes(paramTypes(c), paramTypes(top.head))))
769	        Some(analyzer.meet(top.map(_._1.arrow.getRange)))
770	      else None
771	    // The first candidate no other is more specific than, or the first where
772	    // each has one more specific.
773	    def callType(cs: List[Ranked]): Type = {
774	      val top = minimal(cs)
775	      (if (groundFamily) tieType(top) else None).getOrElse(top.headOption.getOrElse(cs.head)._1.arrow.getRange)
776	    }
777	    def kept(es: Attempt, coerce: Boolean) = holds(es, coerce) && context.forall(c =>
778	      coercions.substitutableFor(callType(candidatesOf(es)), c))
779	    // Each attempt: whether it is given the context, whether it coerces, and
780	    // the attempt itself.
781	    val attempts: List[(Boolean, Boolean, () => Attempt)] =
782	      if (context.isDefined)
783	        List((false, false, () => applicable(None, false)), (true, false, () => applicable(context, false)),
784	             (true, true, () => applicable(context, true)), (false, true, () => applicable(None, true)))
785	      else List((true, false, () => applicable(None, false)), (true, true, () => applicable(None, true)))
786	    val tried = attempts.to(LazyList).map { case (withContext, coerce, a) => (withContext, coerce, a()) }
787	    val keptAttempt = tried.find { case (_, coerce, a) => kept(a, coerce) }
788	    if (keptAttempt.isEmpty && retry)
789	      retypedApplication(preCandidates, iargs, args, context, mOpName, fallBackWithoutContext).
790	        foreach(r => return Some(r))
791	    val es = keptAttempt.map(_._3).getOrElse {
792	      // No attempt is kept: of the attempts with the context, or for a call
793	      // written f(x) of those without it, the first that holds a candidate,
794	      // whatever its result, and otherwise the first.
795	      val from = tried.filter(_._1 != (fallBackWithoutContext && context.isDefined))
796	      from.find { case (_, coerce, a) => holds(a, coerce) }.getOrElse(from.head)._3
797	    }
798	    val candidates = candidatesOf(es)
799	    val overloadingErrors = es.collect { case (Right(e), _, _) => e }
800	
801	    // If there were no candidates, report errors, and each numeral outside
802	    // the range of a parameter type that would take it.
803	    if (candidates.isEmpty) {
804	      errors.signal(errorFactory.makeApplicationError(overloadingErrors))
805	      signalNumeralRanges(preCandidates, args)
806	      return None
807	    }
808	
809	    // Sort the arrows and instantiations to find the statically most
810	    // applicable. Then update each candidate's Overloading node. The sort and
811	    // the minimal candidates below read one order.
812	    val order = new PartialOrder[Ranked](candidates, moreSpecific)
813	    val sorted = order.linear
814	
815	    // An overloading more specific than every candidate, whose size the call
816	    // does not fix, makes the call an error.
817	    val unfixed = overloadingErrors.filter {
818	      case NoContextError(_, _, Some(u)) => candidates.forall(c => moreSpecificCandidate(u, c._1, None, c._2, false, c._3))
819	      case _ => false
820	    }
821	    if (!unfixed.isEmpty) {
822	      errors.signal(errorFactory.makeApplicationError(unfixed))
823	      return None
824	    }
825	
826	    // Ensure that the head is the most specific: the one candidate no other
827	    // is more specific than.
828	    val top = order.minimal
829	
830	    // A tie whose tied candidates differ only where the argument is a numeral:
831	    // each numeral is read as ZZ32 (ZZ64 or ZZ by magnitude), and the call
832	    // resolves as an argument of that type would, over every candidate: of
833	    // those the readings fit, the ones they fit without coercion first. At a
834	    // position whose declared type is a bare type parameter, a reading fits a
835	    // candidate compared on its declared arrow by that parameter's bound.
836	    def numeralTie(): Option[Ranked] = {
837	      val exprs = args.map(_.left.toOption)
838	      val n = exprs.size
839	      if (top.exists(c => paramTypes(c).size != n)) return None
840	      val tiedTypes = top.map(paramTypes)
841	      val differ = (0 until n).filter(i =>
842	        tiedTypes.exists(t => !Formula.isTrue(analyzer.equivalent(t(i), tiedTypes.head(i))))).toList
843	      if (differ.isEmpty || !differ.forall(i => exprs(i).exists(isNumeral))) return None
844	      val readings = (0 until n).toList.flatMap(i => exprs(i).filter(isNumeral).map(e => (i, numeralReading(List(e)))))
845	      if (readings.exists(_._2.isEmpty)) return None
846	      // The types a reading must fit at position i of a candidate.
847	      def targets(c: Ranked, i: Int, r: Type): List[Type] = {
848	        val bare = c._2.flatMap { d =>
849	          val sps = getStaticParams(d).filter(sp => !sp.isLifted && sp.getKind.isInstanceOf[KindType])
850	          zipWithDomain(args, d.getDomain).lift(i).map(_._2) match {
851	            case Some(v: VarType) => sps.find(_.getName == v.getName).map { sp =>
852	              object subst extends Walker {
853	                override def walk(node: Any): Any = node match {
854	                  case w: VarType if w.getName == v.getName => r
855	                  case _ => super.walk(node)
856	                }
857	              }
858	              toListFromImmutable(sp.getExtendsClause).map(b => subst(b).asInstanceOf[Type])
859	            }
860	            case _ => None
861	          }
862	        }
863	        bare.getOrElse(List(paramTypes(c)(i)))
864	      }
865	      def fitsBy(c: Ranked, rel: (Type, Type) => Boolean) = readings.forall { case (i, r) =>
866	        targets(c, i, r.get).forall(t => rel(r.get, t)) }
867	      val fits = candidates.filter(fitsBy(_, coercions.substitutableFor))
868	      val unconverted = fits.filter(fitsBy(_, (r, t) => isSubtype(r, t)))
869	      val among = if (unconverted.nonEmpty) unconverted else fits
870	      among.filter(c => !among.exists(d => !(d eq c) && moreSpecific(d, c))) match {
871	        case List(c) => Some(c)
872	        case _ => None
873	      }
874	    }
875	
876	    val head: Option[Ranked] =
877	      if (top.size == 1) top.headOption
878	      // A tie among candidates that fit the call as it is, or among candidates
879	      // with one parameter type, keeps the sort's head.
880	      else if (top.isEmpty || !top.exists(counted) ||
881	               top.forall(c => sameTypes(paramTypes(c), paramTypes(top.head)))) sorted.headOption
882	      else numeralTie().orElse {
883	        signalAmbiguity(top.map(c => c._2.getOrElse(c._1.arrow)), args)
884	        return None
885	      }
886	    Some((head.toList.map(_._1) ++ sorted.filterNot(c => head.exists(_ eq c)).map(_._1),
887	          tieType(top).getOrElse(head.getOrElse(sorted.head)._1.arrow.getRange)))
888	  }

890	  /**
891	   * The argument retry, for a call that no attempt keeps, an argument of
892	   * which is itself a call whose static args it inferred with no expected
893	   * type. Each candidate in turn: each such argument is checked again with
894	   * the candidate's parameter type at its position as its expected type, that
895	   * type instantiated, where the candidate has static parameters, by the other
896	   * arguments (writesStaticArgs) and the call's expected type alone; the call is then checked
897	   * against that candidate alone, and the candidate counts when the call's
898	   * type converts to the expected type. Of the candidates that count, the one
899	   * more specific on its declared parameter types than every other is kept,
900	   * with its arguments. Otherwise the call is refused as it was.
901	   */
902	  private def retypedApplication(preCandidates: List[PreAppCandidate],
903	                                 iargs: List[Expr],
904	                                 args: List[Either[Expr, FnExpr]],
905	                                 context: Option[Type],
906	                                 mOpName: Option[Op],
907	                                 fallBackWithoutContext: Boolean)
908	                                (implicit errorFactory: ApplicationErrorFactory)
909	                                 : Option[(List[AppCandidate], Type)] = {
910	    val positions = args.zipWithIndex.collect { case (Left(c), i) if retypable(c) => i }.toSet
911	    if (positions.isEmpty || iargs.size != args.size) return None
912	    val tryChecker = STypeCheckerFactory.makeTryChecker(this)
913	    def same(a: Expr, b: Expr) = Formula.isTrue(analyzer.equivalent(getType(a).get, getType(b).get))
914	    val found = preCandidates.flatMap { pc =>
915	      val domain =
916	        if (!hasStaticParams(pc.arrow)) Some(pc.arrow.getDomain)
917	        else {
918	          val tys = args.zipWithIndex.map {
919	            case (Left(e), i) if !positions(i) || writesStaticArgs(iargs(i)) => Some(getType(e).get)
920	            case _ => None
921	          }
922	          def constraint(inf: ArrowType, ops: Map[Op, Op]): CFormula =
923	            Formula.and(context.map(c => analyzer.subtype(inf.getRange, c)).toList ++
924	                        zipWithDomain(tys, inf.getDomain).collect { case (Some(t), d) => analyzer.subtype(t, d) })
925	          inferStaticParamsHelper(pc.arrow, constraint, false, true, true).map(_._1.getDomain)
926	        }
927	      domain.toList.flatMap { dom =>
928	        val params = zipWithDomain(args, dom).map(_._2)

(* The other operand fixes a numeral's type at =: a numeral and an NN32, NN64 or RR32 of one value are equal, in either order. *)
component XXXNumeralEqualsNumberWalk
export Executable

run(): () = do
    u0: NN32 = 0
    w0: NN64 = 0
    f0: RR32 = 0
    assert(u0 = 0, "u = 0 for an NN32 zero")
    assert(0 = u0, "0 = u for an NN32 zero")
    assert(w0 = 0, "an NN64 and a numeral of one value are equal, the NN64 first")
    assert(0 = w0, "a numeral and an NN64 of one value are equal, the numeral first")
    assert(f0 = 0, "r = 0 for an RR32 zero")
    println "PASS"
  end

end
(* The library's =/= between a number and a numeral answers NOT of their =. *)
component XXXNotEqualNumeral
export Executable

run(): () = do
    w: ZZ32 = 0
    u: NN32 = w.asNN32
    v: NN64 = w.asNN64
    d: RR64 = 0.0
    r: RR32 = narrow(d)
    q: QQ = 1/2
    assert(NOT (u =/= 0), "opr-overview.tex, the sentence on e =/= e' that closes subsection \"GCD, LCM, and CHOOSE Operators\": e =/= e' is NOT (e = e'), and numbers.tex, section \"Rational Numbers\": a zero NN32 = 0")
    assert(NOT (v =/= 0), "opr-overview.tex, the sentence on e =/= e' that closes subsection \"GCD, LCM, and CHOOSE Operators\": e =/= e' is NOT (e = e'), and numbers.tex, section \"Rational Numbers\": a zero NN64 = 0")
    assert(NOT (r =/= 0), "opr-overview.tex, the sentence on e =/= e' that closes subsection \"GCD, LCM, and CHOOSE Operators\": e =/= e' is NOT (e = e'), and numbers.tex, section \"Rational Numbers\": a zero RR32 = 0")
    assert(NOT (q =/= 0.5), "opr-overview.tex, the sentence on e =/= e' that closes subsection \"GCD, LCM, and CHOOSE Operators\": e =/= e' is NOT (e = e'), and numbers.tex, section \"Rational Numbers\": the QQ 1/2 = 0.5")

  end

cd /home/user/fortress-numeral-most-specific/ProjectFortress/compiler_tests && cat > NumeralMostSpecificCompiled.fss <<'EOF'
(* A numeral at a call goes to the most specific declaration that takes it, by its own conversion if need be; its default is the last resort. *)
component NumeralMostSpecificCompiled
export Executable

k(x: Any): String = "any"
k(x: NN32): String = "nn32"

same(a: Any, b: Any): String = "any"
same(a: NN32, b: NN32): String = "nn32"

gg[\T extends Number\](x: ZZ32, y: T): String = "zz32"
gg(x: Any, y: Any): String = "any"

run(): () = do
    u: NN32 = 0
    a: Any = u
    w: ZZ64 = 4
    x: RR64 = 1.3
    e: RR64 = 3.0
    assert(k(5), "nn32", "conversions-coercions.tex, section \"Coercion\": the numeral's own conversion reaches the more specific declaration")
    assert(same(u, 0), "nn32", "the numeral second, beside an NN32")
    assert(same(0, u), "nn32", "the numeral first, beside an NN32")
    assert(k(a), "any", "a value typed Any runs the declaration over Any")
    assert(same(a, 0), "any", "a value typed Any fixes no type for the numeral beside it")
    assert(gg(5, w), "zz32", "the declaration that the numeral's default fits is the more specific")
    assert(x^2 = x x, "an RR64 to a numeral power")
    assert(x^3 = x (x x), "the integer power of an RR64 multiplies: the numeral exponent is a ZZ32")
    assert(NOT (x^3 = x^e), "the RR64 exponent's power rounds otherwise")
    println("PASS")
  end

end
EOF
cat > NumeralMostSpecificCompiled.test <<'EOF'
tests=NumeralMostSpecificCompiled
link
run
run_out_contains=PASS
EOF

One way to think about coercion is that if type \VAR{T} can be coerced
to type \VAR{U}, then a value of type \VAR{T} can be used to ``stand
in'' for a value of type \VAR{U} in a functional call, for example.  This is
different from actually \emph{being} of type \VAR{U}; it means only
that, given any value of type \VAR{T}, an appropriate value of type
\VAR{U} can be computed to substitute for it.  Also, coercion occurs
only when the declared type of the corresponding parameter in the
functional declaration is exactly the type \VAR{U} being coerced to
 not if it is a supertype of \VAR{U}.  Note, however, that if type
 \VAR{T} can be coerced to type \VAR{U} then any subtype of \VAR{T}
 can also be coerced to type \VAR{U}.

A numeral's conversion into its default (\secref{literals}) is not a coercion,
and applies where coercion does not: where the declared type is a supertype of
the default, as \TYP{Any}, \TYP{Object} and \TYP{Number} are, or is a type
parameter declared without a bound, and where no type is declared.
At a call, a numeral is applicable without coercion to a parameter of its
default type and to a parameter of a type that fixes no type for it; its
conversion into any other type is a coercion
(\secref{applicability-with-coercion}).
So of the declarations \EXP{h(x\COLON\mathbb{Z}32)} and
\EXP{h(x\COLON\TYP{Any})}, both applicable to \EXP{h(5)} without coercion, the
call invokes the first, which is the more specific.
A numeral at a type of a program's own that declares no coercion from the
numeral's type is not converted into its default and then coerced, since
coercion does not chain (below); it is a static error.

content.content:
## The checker's time

This section is for a change of the checker: its Scala under `scala_src/`, or `ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast` and the generators under `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/astgen/`, from which the build generates the checker's syntax tree and `Walker`.

The count stage takes `<out-file> <scratch>` and about 80 to 180 seconds, more under load. It can run past the Bash tool's 120-second limit, so run it in the background (`session.md`). It writes a table to the out-file: the errors of each api, the total, the number of places with errors, and the first crash. It keeps the checker's whole output in `<scratch>/run.txt`, and its caches in `<scratch>`, so a run from the base build leaves the base build as it was.

The checker checks every api first, and the component only if no api has an error. In each api or component, it stops at the first of its stages that finds errors. The stages run in this order (`compiler/StaticChecker.java`, `checkCompilationUnit`):

1. The type hierarchy and the type check.
2. The overloading check, which also compares the overloads' return types.
3. In the component only, the export check (`library.md`, "Designing a change").

So the count misses the errors of the later stages, and a fix of an early error can raise it.

The table's rows tell a clean run from a run that the checker did not finish:

- `#total 0` and `#locations 0`: the checker reached the component and found no error.
- `#stopped`, in place of `#total` and `#locations`: the errors came from a phase before the checker, such as the parse. The checker reported none and did not reach the component. The script exits 1, and the gate reads the table as red.
- `#crash`: the first crash of the overloading check that the run survived, or `none`.

If the run printed no error total and was not clean, the script writes no table and exits 1.

The checker's results are the programs that it accepts and refuses, and each error with its text and its place. On the interpreter's library, a change keeps the results the same if both of these hold:

- The two tables are equal: `diff` prints nothing.
- The two `run.txt` files are equal after you replace each run's own tree path with one word, such as `TREE`. Any difference fails.

A node's hash starts from its class name, so an order in the output, such as the apis' checks, does not vary from run to run. A moved order is a difference: keep the old order, or report it.

`Walker`, in the generated `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/nodes/FortressAst.scala`, is split into methods under 8,000 bytes of bytecode. HotSpot does not compile a longer method, and the walker runs on every node. `MethodSizeJUTest` fails if a method of the build grows past the limit, except the methods that its source lists in `listed(...)` entries. Run it alone with `ant testOnly -DtestPattern=MethodSizeJUTest`. If a method of `Walker` fails, lower `WALKER_CASES_PER_METHOD` in `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/astgen/ScalaAstGenerator.java`. If another method fails, split it under the limit. List it only if nothing in the checker or a compiled run calls it, with its size and what runs it, and name it in your report.

The timing is a smoke test, to catch a slowdown of several times. One run of each tree is enough. A small difference, or one within the noise from run to run, is not a finding. In your report, say what you saw, and do not analyse it.

If you change the checker:

1. Make the change correct, with its tests. Commit it, and name the commit in your report.
2. Time the base build and the change, named `base` and `change`. Run the base in a call set up for the base build (`build-and-caches.md`), and the change in a call set up for your tree, each in the background (`session.md`). Use the same command for both, with `N` the run's name:

       export W=<your tree> N=base ; mkdir -p $W/tmp/count
       time explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh $W/tmp/count/$N.txt $W/tmp/count/$N

3. Make a second pass that makes the checker faster. Start with a profile (below). Where the profile shows a gain, take it. Where it shows none, say so in your report, with the profile's top frames.
4. If the second pass changed code, run the count stage once more with the command of step 2, named `pass`. Show that its results are the same as `change`'s. Then run `ant testQuick` once more (`tests-running.md`, "When to run a whole suite"). If it changed nothing, run neither, and report `change`'s results in place of `pass`'s.
5. If the pass reuses an answer that the checker computed earlier, as a memo does, audit it on one full run. Put the audit in an instrumented copy ("Testing an edit here"), never in the tree. In the audit, compute each reused answer again and compare the two. If any answer differs, the reuse is wrong: fix it or drop it, then repeat step 4. Report the count of reuses and of differences.
6. In your report, give each run's seconds, the diff of the `base` and `change` tables, the comparison of their `run.txt` files, and that `pass` has the same results as `change`.

#!/bin/bash
# The gate's checker-count stage: run the bytecode compiler's static checker over the
# INTERPRETER's library, with the interpreter's prelude in scope, and print the per-api
# error table, the total and the crash line that follows it.
#
# Why it exists: POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-21, "the library route" - one library, the
# interpreter's, becomes the library the compiler checks - and step 1 of
# coordinator/library-route-judgement.md, which makes the distance to that goal a
# permanent gate stage rather than a one-off script. A change in the count is reported, not red (checker-gate-review.md).
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched:
# javac output and the checker's caches go to the scratch directory (default: $TMPDIR
# or /tmp), and the caches are given to the JVM as -Dfortress.caches, honoured through
# ProjectProperties.java:261-269,283, so default_repository/ is never read or written.
# Exit 0 if the table holds a total; 1 if no table could be produced, or if the table holds
# no total because the run's errors are not the checker's (#stopped, below). 20 s in the
# main tree, measured 2026-09-22; it needs no library rebuild and no warm cache.
#
# The run stops after the type checker (WorldFlip -stop check), since 2026-10-24 (climb batch
# 22): the compiler's own phase order up to and including TYPECHECK, integer literal folding
# included, as the distance stage's DistanceMulti -order check. Past the checker, the code
# generator's refusals are not the checker's errors (FACTS F-34 counts them), and its first
# one throws, so a run on a library the checker passes went on into the code generator and
# printed no total. A run the checker stops runs the same phases as before; a clean check,
# a run that reached the component's check and ended rc 0 with no error line, reads as 0.
#
# The two sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-22 from
# explorations/perf-probes/prelude/, so that the gate does not depend on a probe
# directory: WorldFlip.java (Shell.useInterpreterLibraries() plus
# PhaseOrder.compilerPhaseOrder, both public, which is the world switch without an edit
# to a tracked file; its -stop check added 2026-10-24) and shadow-src/.../StaticChecker.java, a copy of
# ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java with three
# instrumentation points added: it names each compilation unit it checks and prints that
# unit's error count, and it catches the OverloadingChecker crash instead of dying on it.
# It is put AHEAD of ProjectFortress/build on the classpath, the technique of
# perf-probes/prelude/run-all.sh:33-35. A copy of a tracked source goes stale silently,
# so the checksum of the tracked one is recorded here and the table's "#shadow" line
# says whether it still matches.
#
# The overloading checker's memo is off (-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false, read
# at OverloadingChecker.scala:77), since 2026-09-27 (climb batch 7). The memo is keyed on
# declaration pairs and hides 27 to 35 errors depending on the build order once an api's
# overloading check runs (perf-probes/nat/triage.md section 1; FACTS.md, "The hidden
# layer, classified"); with it off every build gives one count. The table's "#cache"
# row says so. On the tree of 2026-09-27 the count is 62 with the memo on and off,
# because the FortressLibrary api stops before its overloading check.
#
# The table, tab-separated, every row tagged:
#   #api        one row per api the checker checked, with that api's error count
#   #total      the errors that the run's last "File X has N errors." line counts, or 0 for
#               a clean check (above)
#   #locations  the distinct file:line those errors were reported at
#   #stopped    in place of #total and #locations, when that line counts errors that the
#               checker did not report: no api's check reported an error and the checker

#               binding, before the apis' check or between it and the component's. It names

1	# The specification
2	
3	Three folders hold the team's specification:
4	
5	- `Specification/` is the team's text, as the revival revises it. It says what the language means, except where a decision of the curator says otherwise.
6	- `Specification-1.0-frozen/` is the unrevised copy. Cite it as "the Working Draft of February 2011". Only `fortress.1.0.pdf` in it is the 1.0 release. Leave this copy unchanged.
7	- `Documentation/Specification/` is the team's later restart, which they did not finish. If its Types chapter, `Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick`, covers a topic, cite it beside `Specification/` as the designers' later word.
8	
9	Appendix I, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, records the changes to the text. Its revival section has one entry for each change that the revival made.
10	
11	A draft build prints the team's `\note{}` boxes, and a release build hides them. Many say that a feature was not built, for example "Reduction variables are not yet supported." Before you record a missing feature as a gap, grep the notes of its chapter: `grep -n '\\note{' Specification/<file>.tex`.
12	
13	The api listings of the library part are generated from the library's `.fsi` files when the specification is built (`Specification/library/apis/`, not in the tree). A listing shows the library itself, so it cannot justify a change of the library. Cite the `.fsi` file.
14	
15	To weigh the specification against the team's later texts, or to find the designers' reason for a rule, read `exploring.md`, "Weighing the sources".
16	
17	## Changing the text: the revision form
18	
19	Every change of the text has the four parts below, so that no disagreement between the text and an implementation stays hidden.
20	
21	1. An entry in the revival section of Appendix I: a `\subsection` with a `\seclabel`. The entry gives:
22	   - the affected sections, the change, its rationale and its effect. The effect names each departure: each way in which walk or the compiled path does not do what the new text says, with its ledger row.
23	   - the original text, quoted with its path and line in `Specification-1.0-frozen/`;
24	   - what a reversal to the alternative not taken would need;
25	   - the decision of the curator that it follows (its POSITIONS entry), or the reason that your brief gives.
26	
27	   For the form, print one entry, about 2 KB: `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'doc:Specification/appendices/changes.tex#choice of a coercion'`.
28	
29	2. At each changed passage, a callout that prints in every build, unlike a `\note`:
30	
31	       \revision{<label>}{<what changed, in a sentence or two>}
32	
33	   `<label>` is the `\seclabel` of the entry. `Specification/fortress/fortress.tex` defines `\revision`.
34	
35	3. The front matter's one paragraph on the revision, in `Specification/fortress/preamble.tex`. If your change makes it false, correct it.
36	
37	4. The full reasoning, in `decision-record.md` in the folder of your work under `explorations/`: each changed passage, the original and the new text, the reason, and the way back. For the form, print one passage of an earlier record, about 4 KB: `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/compile-ladder/rung-spec-route-a/decision-record.md#3.3'`.
38	
39	If the revision refuses an example, keep the example in the text, marked "Not allowed", as the specification itself does. If your change contradicts a calculus of Appendix A, keep the calculus's rules and soundness claims. Add a callout to it that says what it predates.
40	
41	Check each changed sentence of `Specification/` or `Documentation/` against the curator's decisions. If it says what walk or the compiled path does, run a program that shows it.
42	
43	## Building it
44	
45	To check your LaTeX, build the specification in a built tree, after the setup lines. It takes about 90 s, so start it detached (`session.md`, "Long commands"):
46	
47	    nohup bash -c '( cd Specification/fortress && ./ant genSource && ./ant tex ) > tmp/spec.txt 2>&1; echo EXIT=$? >> tmp/spec.txt' >/dev/null 2>&1 &
48	
49	- Both commands must end in `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, and `grep -c 'LaTeX Warning: Reference\|LaTeX Warning: Label .* multiply defined\|LaTeX Warning: There were multiply-defined labels\|^! Undefined control sequence' Specification/fortress/fortress.log` must print 0.
50	- If `pdflatex` is missing, install the packages of the `PKGS` line of `explorations/experiment/setup.sh` with `apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y`.
51	- The build writes only ignored files, its log among them, which can reach 400 MB. Remove them afterwards: `git clean -fXq -- Specification`.
52	- Update `Specification/fortress.pdf` only if your brief asks for it: copy `Specification/fortress/fortress.pdf` over it.
53	
54	## When the text and an implementation disagree
55	
56	- If a decision of the curator says which side is correct, the other side is wrong. If the wrong side is in your area, change it to agree. If not, record the departure as `tests-writing.md`, "How a defect is recorded", says.
57	- If no decision says so, the disagreement is a conflict. Switch to exploring (`exploring.md`).
58	- If the passage has an Appendix I entry, name the departure or the conflict in the entry's effect, with its ledger row. Then the text claims no more than holds.
59	
60	## Citing it
61	
62	- If your change renames or removes a section that a test names, update that citation in the same commit.
63	- Inside the text, cite a section with `\secref{label}`.

1	# Committing and pushing
2	
3	**scratch**
4	: Files and folders that your work makes and `main` does not keep: logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, probe programs, lists and private caches folders.
5	
6	Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.
7	
8	## What to commit
9	
10	- Commit your change, its tests, your report if it is a file, and any reusable script.
11	- Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records. A row's close follows the fix's commit (`records.md`).
12	- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
13	- In a fresh clone, `.claude/worktrees/` and `.claude/agents/` show as untracked, because the lines of `.git/info/exclude` that hide them are not in the clone. Do not commit them.
14	- Keep a copyrighted PDF or deck in `research/decks/`, which is gitignored. Cite it by its Wayback URL. Notes on it go in `research/extracts/`: your own summary, with brief attributed quotations.
15	- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.
16	- Name a model by its tier (Opus, Sonnet, Fable) in any text that you commit, commit messages included. Never write its model identifier, the API's name for the model, which starts with `claude-`.
17	
18	## How to commit
19	
20	Commit as you go, each commit in one command that names its paths:
21	
22	    git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>
23	
24	- The command commits only the paths that it names. Other agents may have uncommitted edits in your tree. Leave them alone.
25	- If you renamed a file with `git mv`, name its old path in `git commit` only, because `git add` refuses a path that no longer exists: `git add -- <new paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <new paths> <old paths>`.
26	- Never commit a copied directory, and never use `git add -A`.
27	- Before you commit more than a few hundred lines, stage them and read what you staged: `git add -- <paths> && git diff --cached --stat -- <paths>`.
28	- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
29	- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests:
30	
31	      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
32	      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB
33	
34	  If your brief gives another session line, use it. If a commit that is already made has a footer that names a model, by any name or identifier, leave the commit as it is. Such a footer is not a defect: do not check for it, report it or list it.
35	
36	## Pushing
37	
38	Push after every commit, so that a lost container loses nothing.
39	
40	- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`. Your brief says how the branch reaches `main`.
41	- From a session in a cloud container, do not try to delete a branch on GitHub, or retry a refusal with another tool (the `cloud-container` skill, "Rules for every agent"). Removing a worktree does not delete its branch, which stays. Ask nobody in your report to delete a branch.

#!/bin/bash
# The plan review's probe of 2026-11-10: the compiled checker, by the distance stage's own
# driver and shadows (explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/), over components that the
# stage does not list, against the one library.  Run in a seeded worktree, never in the main
# tree or a base build, with the fortress-repo skill's setup lines in the shell:
#
#     run.sh <check|full> <out-dir> <dir to run in> <targets...>
#
# The first target should be Library/FortressLibrary.fss, by its absolute path, so that the
# library's apis are checked once with every stage; each later target is checked with its
# component only.  <out-dir>/run.txt holds the driver's whole output: one "@@SC ERR" line
# for each error, "@@TC COMPONENT name errors=N" for each target (N counts an error once for
# each stage that reports it), and with "full" one "@@CG OK|FAIL|PREFAIL" line for each
# declaration that the code generator met.  Nothing in the tree is written: the shadows, the
# caches and the JVM's temporary folder are under <tree>/tmp and <out-dir>.
set -u
ORDER=$1; OUT=$2; CWD=$3; shift 3
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:?set FORTRESS_HOME to the worktree}
D=$FH/explorations/coordinator/tools/distance
S=$FH/tmp/model-closure-shadows
mkdir -p "$S/shadow-src" "$S/shadow-classes" "$S/classes" "$OUT/caches" "$OUT/tmp"
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | sed 's#:[^:]*/default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache##')
if [ ! -f "$S/classes/DistanceMulti.class" ]; then
  ( cd "$FH" && python3 "$D/shadow-patch.py" ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress "$S/shadow-src" \
             && python3 "$D/add-patch.py" "$S/shadow-src" ) > "$S/shadows.txt" 2>&1 || { echo "a shadow edit no longer matches; see $S/shadows.txt"; exit 1; }
  F=$S/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress
  javac -nowarn -encoding UTF-8 -cp "$CP" -d "$S/shadow-classes" "$F/compiler/StaticChecker.java" \
        "$F/compiler/phases/TypeCheckPhase.java" "$F/compiler/phases/DesugarPhase.java" \
        "$F/compiler/phases/CodeGenerationPhase.java" "$F/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java" \
        "$F/compiler/Desugarer.java" "$F/nodes_util/NodeComparator.java" >> "$S/shadows.txt" 2>&1 || { echo "the shadows do not compile; see $S/shadows.txt"; exit 1; }
  javac -nowarn -cp "$CP" -d "$S/classes" "$D/DistanceMulti.java" >> "$S/shadows.txt" 2>&1 || { echo "the driver does not compile"; exit 1; }
fi
FLAGS="-Dprobe.tolerant=true -Dprobe.all=true -Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false"
[ "$ORDER" = full ] && FLAGS="$FLAGS -Dprobe.bottomCompare=true -Dprobe.skipOverloads=true -Dprobe.dumpErrors=true"
cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg > "$OUT/load.txt"
( cd "$CWD" && timeout -k 30 3000 java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow -Djava.io.tmpdir="$OUT/tmp" \
      -Dfortress.caches="$OUT/caches" $FLAGS -cp "$S/shadow-classes:$S/classes:$CP" DistanceMulti -order "$ORDER" -setting any "$@" ) > "$OUT/run.txt" 2>&1
echo "rc=$?" >> "$OUT/run.txt"
rm -rf "$OUT/caches" "$OUT/tmp"
grep '^### \|@@TC COMPONENT' "$OUT/run.txt" | cut -c1-160
component NumeralLine
export Executable
lr0: RR64 = 0.01
nSteps: ZZ32 = 1000
learningRate(s: ZZ32): RR64 = lr0 (1 - (1.0 s) / nSteps)
half(s: ZZ32): RR64 = (1.0 s) / 2
scaled(s: ZZ32): RR64 = 1.0 s
run(): () = println learningRate(3)
end
NumeralLine.fss
SingleTop.fss
TupleTopPlain.fss
run.sh

content.content:
## The ladder regression

The compile ladder records how far each test program gets through the compiler's phases, in order: parse, disambiguate, typecheck, codegen, link, run and pass. The ladder regression runs part of it again, and compares the result with the baseline, `explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/`:

- It compiles and runs the 85 programs of the baseline's `pass-list.txt`. It compares each one's phase and output with the baseline's `raw/`.
- It compiles the eighteen components of the two microGPT programs, and never runs them. It compares each one's phase with the baseline's `microgpt-phase.md`.

A file that moved gets a mark:

- DOWN: a phase lower than the record.
- MISSING: a file with no output.
- STDOUT: output that differs from the record after the `Operation took <n>ms` line is masked.
- UP: a phase higher than the record. This is progress, not red.

DOWN, MISSING and STDOUT are red, unless your brief declared that move as expected before the gate ran.
Warning: do not run `run-ladder.sh`, the driver over every test program, with its defaults. Its default root is shared, its cache pruning corrupts a parallel run, and its default `OUT` is a tracked folder.

To run it, as step 7, with step 3's copies of the caches:

1. Copy the drivers into `tmp/gate/ladder/`, and point their outputs and caches there:

       D=$PWD/tmp/gate/ladder ; B=explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19
       cp explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/run-subset.sh \
          $B/classify.py $B/microgpt-phase.sh $B/microgpt-phase.py $D/
       sed -i -e "s|^OUT=.*|OUT=$D|" -e "s|^LADDER_ROOT=.*|LADDER_ROOT=$D/root|" $D/run-subset.sh
       sed -i -e "s|/home/user/fortress|$PWD|g" \
           -e "s|^export LADDER_CACHES=.*|export LADDER_CACHES=$D/root/ladder-caches|" \
           -e "s|^export LADDER_TMP=.*|export LADDER_TMP=$D/root/ladder-tmp|" \
           -e "s|^RAW=.*|RAW=$D/raw/microgpt|" -e "s|^TSV=.*|TSV=$D/microgpt-results.tsv|" $D/microgpt-phase.sh
       tail -n +2 $B/pass-list.txt | cut -f1 | sed 's|/|\t|' > $D/subset.txt

2. Run the four scripts, with no arguments, in this order: `bash $D/run-subset.sh`, `python3 $D/classify.py`, `bash $D/microgpt-phase.sh` and `python3 $D/microgpt-phase.py`. Each reads and writes in `$D`. This takes about 200 s for the 85 and 35 s for the eighteen, so run them in the background (`session.md`, "Long commands"). With step 3's copies, the driver skips the library's build (about 145 s).
3. Compare: `ladder_compare $B $D`, then `diff <(mg_phases $B/microgpt-phase.md) <(mg_phases $D/microgpt-phase.md)`. Append each line that they print to the summary, with `# ladder ` before it.

If your brief asks for your change's own ladder subset, write your own `subset.txt`. Put in it each file whose recorded first error in the baseline's `raw/` names something that your change touched. Run them after your edit only. Compare them with the newest landed `ladder.tsv`, or with the baseline's `raw/` for a file that the gate does not run.

151:MicroGPT runs only under walk, by hand, never in the gate. Check the model when your brief asks for it: run your tree's `explorations/coordinator/tools/mg-run.sh <work-dir> <label> [threads]`. `<work-dir>` is a folder under your tree's `tmp/`, and `threads` sets `FORTRESS_THREADS`, 1 by default. The script runs the quick pair at once, `MicroGptFlatQuick.fss` and `MicroGptAplQuick.fss`: two forward and backward passes each, against the reference values, in about 56 s for both. Each starts from an empty private cache and writes `<work-dir>/<name>.txt`. Read its `VERDICT:` line and its last line, `rc=`.
153:- Add the word `full` only if your brief asks for it. It runs the full pair, `MicroGptFlatCheck.fss` and `MicroGptAplCheck.fss`, with 40 checks each and a 90-minute timeout.
